children: Lenovo Group Limited
LNVGY is currently trading at a forward price-to-sales multiple of 0.40, lower than the industry average of 8.69 but higher than the median of 0.19 over five years. It has a Value Score of A.

Lenovo Group is a global technology leader with a diversified portfolio spanning PCs, enterprise infrastructure and intelligent solutions. The company is well-positioned to benefit from the enterprise PC refresh cycle, growing adoption of AI-enabled devices and rising investments in AI infrastructure worldwide.
Lenovo Group trades at a discount to the technology industry, likely because investors still view it primarily as a low-margin, cyclical PC maker, while also pricing in China and geopolitical risks.

Dell Technologies
DELL but a bit expensive compared to
HP Inc
. HPQ.
Price Outperformance
Shares of Lenovo Group have skyrocketed 225.8% year to date, outperforming the industry, the sector, as well as the Zacks S&P 500 composite.
LNVGY vs Industry, Sector, S&P 500 YTD
While Dell Technologies surged 262.8%, HP Inc. gained 42.8% in the same time frame.
The Case for Lenovo Group

Lenovo Group remains one of the world’s largest PC manufacturers, but its evolution into a diversified technology company is improving its long-term growth prospects. Expansion into higher-margin areas—including AI infrastructure, hybrid cloud, enterprise services and AI-enabled devices—is reducing its reliance on the cyclical PC market and creating additional earnings streams.

The Intelligent Devices Group remains a major cash generator, supported by commercial PC replacement cycles, demand for premium products and growing adoption of AI PCs. Meanwhile, the Infrastructure Solutions Group is becoming an important growth driver as demand rises for AI servers, data-center infrastructure and high-performance computing. An AI server pipeline exceeding $21 billion provides solid revenue visibility.

Lenovo is also expanding its enterprise AI capabilities. Its Hybrid AI Advantage solutions, developed with NVIDIA, help enterprises deploy scalable, real-time AI inferencing across cloud and on-premise environments. Moreover, the acquisition of Infinidat strengthens Lenovo’s presence in high-end enterprise storage, broadens its infrastructure portfolio and offers opportunities for revenue growth and margin improvement.

The company’s diversified presence across Asia, Europe and the Americas limits dependence on any single market. Longstanding relationships with enterprises, governments and channel partners further reinforce its competitive position.

Lenovo continues to invest in Personal AI and Enterprise AI as it seeks to become a full-stack AI leader. Disciplined cost management, healthy cash generation, a prudent balance sheet and consistent dividends should support innovation and long-term shareholder returns.

However, global PC shipments declined 2% in the fiscal first quarter of 2027, although Lenovo retained its leadership with a 25.6% market share. Rising memory prices, fueled by strong AI data-center demand, could put pressure on PC and server margins. The U.S.-China trade tensions also present risks, potentially increasing costs or restricting access to key technologies and markets.
Growth Projections for Lenovo

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal 2027 revenues indicates a 31.5% year-over-year increase, while that for earnings suggests a 66.1% year-over-year increase. The consensus estimate for fiscal 2028 revenues indicates a 19.7% year-over-year increase, while that for earnings suggests an increase of 58.4% year over year.
Lenovo has a Growth Score of A.
Optimistic Analyst Sentiment on LNVGY
The consensus estimates for fiscal 2027 and 2028 earnings have moved 26.3% and 55.6% north, respectively, in the past 30 days, reflecting analysts' optimism.
The consensus estimates for fiscal 2027 and 2028 earnings of Dell Technologies have moved north in the past 30 days.
Estimates for HP Inc.’s fiscal 2026 and 2027 earnings have also moved north in the past 30 days.
Parting Thoughts on LNVGY Shares

Powered by its hybrid AI strategy, operational excellence and relentless innovation, management is confident in sustaining Lenovo’s growth momentum and driving long-term profitability. Management aims to become a $100 billion company within two years through operational excellence and continued innovation in Personal AI and Enterprise AI. Its VGM Score of A further reinforces its growth appeal.
